items.title: Hydrogen is folding the CLI into the Oxygen deploy path
items.body:
Three PRs in eight days move deploy configuration out of hydrogen.config.ts and into a new oxygen.toml read directly by the platform. The CLI still writes the file, but it is no longer the thing that performs the deploy — that moved server-side.

For us this closes a question we have carried since the Turtle Beach build: whether to wrap the Hydrogen CLI in our own deploy tooling. Wrapping a CLI that is becoming a file generator buys nothing. The integration point to build against is oxygen.toml.

items.title: Oxygen worker runtime has gone quiet
items.body:
Thirty-four days with no commits, after fifty-one consecutive weeks with at least one. The last merged PR was a dependency bump. No deprecation notice, no RFC, no issue explaining it.

Silence is ambiguous and worth saying so: it precedes a rewrite about as often as a wind-down, and we cannot tell which from the outside. What makes it worth flagging now rather than in a month is that our own Oxygen work is scheduled for Q4 — the cost of being wrong rises after we commit.

context:
## The evidence under each signal

**Hydrogen / Oxygen deploy** — read from PRs #2841, #2847 and #2852, all merged between Jul 22 and Jul 30 by Kelly Ma and Devon Wu. Marked **confirmed** rather than emerging because the config file is already read by the platform in production, not behind a flag. What would move it back down: a revert, or the CLI regaining deploy responsibility in 2026.4.

**Checkout validation hook** — one RFC (#912) and a prototype branch, no shipping milestone. **Emerging**, not confirmed: RFCs at this stage have roughly even odds. What would move it up is a milestone assignment or a second team's review.

**Storefront cart mutation deprecation** — two changelog notes, no timeline, no RFC. **Speculative**, and it may simply be housekeeping.

## Where the reading is contested

Oxygen's silence is the least safe claim here. A maintainer said in a Discord thread that the team is "heads-down," which reads as continuity; the commit record reads as a stop. I have weighted the commit record, because stated intent is cheap and 34 days is not — but that is a judgment, and it is the one most likely to be wrong.

## Carried forward

Both open questions are unresolved this week. The Deno-runtime prediction is **refuted** — Oxygen's runtime work stayed on workerd, which the March call got wrong.

## Ask me about

What the oxygen.toml shift means for our own deploy tooling and what it would change; whether the ecosystem is moving toward or away from the CLI-wrapping bet we nearly made; and what to watch next week to settle the Oxygen question fastest.
